title: Local closed matrix charts for lowest cohomology
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $E\in D(\mathcal O_S)$ be perfect [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex] of Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-pc-derived-tensor-cohomology-vanishes]. Let $r\in\mathbf N$ and let $U\subseteq S$ be open, with inclusion $u$ [def-weil-open-immersion], such that $\beta_a(x)\leq r$ for every $x\in U$ [def-sc-derived-fiber-betti]. For each point $x$ of the open subscheme $U$, there is an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq U$ of $x$, with inclusion $v$, and a closed immersion $i:Z\to V$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], such that for every scheme $T$ and morphism $h:T\to V$, a factorization of $h$ through $i$ exists if and only if $H^a(L(u\circ v\circ h)^*E)$ [def-pc-derived-pullback] is finite locally free of rank $r$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Only one neighbourhood at each point is asserted; no global representative over $U$ or overlap comparison is asserted.

source.place: matrix-chart part of the proof, before gluing

proof.text: For a point x of U take its image in S and the affine bounded finite-free residue model of 0BCD. Shrink its affine neighbourhood inside U. Tor amplitude implies that the derived fibre has zero cohomology below a; the corresponding terms of the prescribed-rank model are zero. Its degree-a term has rank s=beta_a(x), with s<=r by the rank-bound hypothesis. Exact restriction and termwise derived pullback transport the model to the resulting chart.

If s=r, cut out the finitely many entries of the outgoing differential by a quasi-coherent ideal. After every map into this chart, degree-a cohomology is the kernel of that pulled-back matrix. If the matrix vanishes it is free of rank r. Conversely trivialize a rank-r kernel locally on the source. Its inclusion into the first term is a square injective free map; its cokernel has zero dual by 0EWY. Every coordinate of the outgoing matrix factors through the cokernel and is therefore zero. The source map factors through the matrix equations, and these local factors agree by monomorphy.

If s<r, use the empty closed subscheme of the chart. A putative free rank-r kernel inside a free rank-s first term, on a nonempty affine source neighbourhood, yields a square injective rank-r map after adjoining r-s zero target coordinates. The transpose is injective by 0EWY, but annihilates a basis vector of a padded coordinate over this nonzero affine ring. Thus any such source must be empty. Empty sources satisfy both predicates. This uses the residue model at every point, so no upper-semicontinuity neighbourhood argument is needed.

The matrix ideal is generated by a finite set, so the quotient map is of finite presentation; apply RingHom.FinitePresentation.of_surjective and LocallyOfFinitePresentation.SpecMap_iff on the affine chart. The empty closed immersion is locally of finite presentation as well. Rank zero gives a zero first term; if a>b Tor amplitude forces the complex to vanish, and the same construction applies. This finishes only the local chart construction, without gluing different target neighbourhoods.

theorem exists_perfectLowestMatrixCharts
    [∀ T : Scheme.{u}, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace))]
    (S : Scheme.{u})
    [∀ U : S.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory S) (hE : IsPerfect S E) (a b : ℤ)
    (hamp : ∀ F : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace),
      ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → schemeDerivedTensorCohomologyVanishes S E F i)
    (r : ℕ)
    (U : S.Opens) (hU : ∀ x : S, x ∈ U → derivedFiberBetti S E a x ≤ r) :
    ∀ x : U.toScheme, ∃ V : U.toScheme.Opens, x ∈ V ∧
      ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ V.toScheme),
        IsClosedImmersion i ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation i ∧
        (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (h : T ⟶ V.toScheme),
          (∃ g : T ⟶ Z, g ≫ i = h) ↔
            SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
              ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
                (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace)) a).obj
                  ((derivedPullback ((h ≫ V.ι) ≫ U.ι)).obj E)) r)
